original_text: Era et al.~\cite{era2025unsupervised} proposed an unsupervised prompt-generation framework for SAM-based porosity segmentation, reducing the need for manual annotation but remaining prompt-dependent under noisy backgrounds, heavy-tailed defect distributions, and complex morphologies.
injected_text: Era et al.~\cite{era2025unsupervised} proposed a prompt-generation framework for SAM-based porosity segmentation, reducing the need for manual annotation but remaining prompt-dependent under noisy backgrounds, heavy-tailed defect distributions, and complex morphologies.
rationale: The cited paper explicitly presents its method as an 'unsupervised' approach; dropping this qualifier removes the specific methodological detail that justifies the subsequent clause, resulting in a partially supported description of the referenced work.
ground_truth_description: Dropped the 'unsupervised' methodological qualifier from the description of the prompt-generation framework proposed by Era et al.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: Era et al.~\cite{era2025unsupervised} proposed an unsupervised prompt-generation framework for SAM-based porosity segmentation, reducing the need for manual annotation but remaining prompt-dependent under noisy backgrounds, heavy-tailed defect distributions, and complex morphologies.

original_text: and keeping over 99\% of the model frozen
injected_text: and keeping over 88\% of the model frozen
rationale: The paper states the frozen share of SAM twice ('keeping over 99% of the model frozen' in the abstract and 'keeping over 99% of SAM parameters frozen' in the method) and states the complementary trainable share as 'less than 1% of the total parameters'. Changing one occurrence to 88% breaks the parts-of-a-whole relationship twice over: it no longer complements the <1% trainable share, and it contradicts the other 99% statement. Only an existing figure is perturbed.
ground_truth_description: Abstract: frozen share changed 99% -> 88%, so it no longer complements the stated <1% trainable share and disagrees with the 99% restated in the method section.

truth.location_cue: training approximately 4.15M parameters and keeping over 99\% of the model frozen
truth.paired_location: method section: 'keeping over 99% of SAM parameters frozen'; and 'less than $1\%$ of the total parameters'
truth.quantity_label: share of SAM parameters kept frozen (%)

rationale: In the mixture-of-experts update each expert E_i is applied to the projected input W_E x. The injected form applies E_i to the projection matrix W_E and then right-multiplies by x, which is structurally similar but not the same operator: the expert now acts on a matrix rather than on the projected feature vector, and the result no longer matches the architecture the surrounding text describes. Perturbs the existing equation in place.
ground_truth_description: MoE update: expert application changed from E_i(W_E x) to E_i(W_E) x, so the expert acts on the projection matrix instead of the projected input.

truth.full_equation_latex_before: H = W_0 x + W_D \left( \sum_{i=1}^{N} g_i(x)\, E_i(W_E x) \right),
truth.full_equation_latex_after: H = W_0 x + W_D \left( \sum_{i=1}^{N} g_i(x)\, E_i(W_E) x \right),
truth.term_role: expert application to the projected input

original_text: In Stage 2, we further adapt the model to the target AM XCT domain using a reduced learning rate of $8\times10^{-5}$ for an additional 20 epochs while keeping the same batch size.
injected_text: In Stage 2, we further adapt the model to the target AM XCT domain using a reduced learning rate of $8\times10^{-5}$ for an additional 20 epochs while keeping the same batch size (we observed that larger batch sizes degraded inclusion segmentation performance).
rationale: The inserted parenthetical asserts an ablation finding ('we observed that larger batch sizes degraded inclusion segmentation performance') that the Results section does not actually report, introducing an unsupported sub-claim.
ground_truth_description: Added a parenthetical claiming that larger batch sizes degraded inclusion segmentation performance, which is not supported by any evidence in the paper.
